mainTopic: רבי מאיר on a sinful בת כהן disgracing her father, and the משנה and גמרא on how שריפה is carried out and its source.
overview: The גמרא first asks what the opinion that does not use ״אביה״ for a גזירה שוה learns from that word. It answers with רבי מאיר's ברייתא: a בת כהן's sin brings disgrace on her father. רב אשי adds that this is why even a wicked son of a righteous man is called ״רשיעא בר רשיעא״. The גמרא then explains that the line ״זו מצות הנסקלין״ closes the section on סקילה before the next משנה. That משנה describes שריפה: the condemned person's mouth is forced open and a burning wick is thrown inside. רבי יהודה says to use tongs instead of choking, and the חכמים reject a story of a בת כהן burned with branches. The גמרא explains that the wick is made of lead. It learns through a גזירה שוה from עדת קרח or from בני אהרן that שריפה burns the soul while the body stays whole. It explains why we do not learn from the burned bulls. It also explains how ״ואהבת לרעך כמוך״ and the גזירה שוה work together. The amud ends with an אגדה about נדב ואביהוא and begins a teaching of רבי אליעזר that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does he learn from the word 'her father'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the opinion that does not use ״אביה״ for a גזירה שוה learns from the words ״את אביה היא מחללת״.
steps.simpleTranslation: This phrase, 'she profanes her father,' what does he learn from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. It wants to know what this opinion does with the words 'her father' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used the word ״אביה״ to build a גזירה שוה. The opinion that disagrees does not use it that way, so the word seems to have no job for him. The גמרא assumes every word of the תורה teaches something, so it asks what he learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: she profanes, she brings disgrace upon
what does he expound (learn) from it?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack. The גמרא is not saying the opinion is wrong. It only asks what he does with an extra-looking word.

phrases.english: This phrase, 'she profanes her father,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:9

phrases.english: what does he learn from it?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the opinion that doesn't use 'her father' for a גזירה שוה the way רבי עקיבא does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about how רבי עקיבא uses ״אביה״ for a גזירה שוה. It now asks about the opinion that does not use it that way.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the dissenting opinion draws from the word ״אביה״ in ״את אביה היא מחללת״.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: her sin disgraces her father
steps.stepSummary: He needs the word for רבי מאיר's teaching. Her sin turns her father's honor into disgrace, and people curse the one who raised her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא. רבי מאיר used to say: Why does the פסוק say 'she profanes her father'? To teach that if people used to treat him as holy, they now treat him as ordinary. If they used to honor him, they now treat him with contempt. They say: 'Cursed is the one who fathered this one, cursed is the one who raised this one, cursed is the one from whose loins this one came.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״אביה״ is needed for רבי מאיר's lesson. A daughter's sin brings public shame on her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'her father' is not extra. It teaches a real effect of her sin. The father, a כהן who was treated with קדושה and כבוד, now loses that respect. People even curse him for having fathered and raised her.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (the word is used for a different lesson)
as was taught in a ברייתא
why does the פסוק say this?

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a child's public behavior reflects on the parent. רב אשי builds on this in the next step.

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Meir used to say:
Why does the verse say
'she profanes her father'?
That if they used to treat him as holy,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the father. He is a כהן, so people treated him with special holiness.

phrases.english: they now treat him as ordinary;
if with honor, they now treat him with contempt.
They say: 'Cursed is the one who fathered this one,
cursed is the one who raised this one,
cursed is the one from whose loins this one came.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by giving the word ״אביה״ its own lesson.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word teaches רבי מאיר's lesson. The daughter's sin brings disgrace on her father, who loses his holiness and honor in people's eyes and is cursed.

steps.title: רב אשי: the source for 'wicked son of a wicked one'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the custom of calling even a wicked son of a righteous man ״רשיעא בר רשיעא״ follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: According to whom do we call someone 'a wicked one, son of a wicked one,' even a wicked person whose father is righteous? According to whom? According to this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי connects רבי מאיר's teaching to a common way of speaking. Even when the father is righteous, a wicked son is called 'wicked, son of a wicked one.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it seems unfair to call a righteous father wicked. But רבי מאיר taught that a child's sins bring shame on the parent. So the son's wickedness 'rubs off' on the father's name, and the phrase fits even here.

keyTerms.meaning: a wicked one, son of a wicked one
a sage of the משנה period

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a child's sin disgraces the parent. רב אשי: that is why even a wicked son of a righteous man is called ״רשיעא בר רשיעא״.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
According to whom do we call someone 'a wicked one, son of a wicked one,'
even a wicked one who is the son of a righteous one? According to whom?
According to this תנא.
phrases.notes: 'This תנא' is רבי מאיר from the ברייתא just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי מאיר's ברייתא and applies its idea to a common expression.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calling a wicked son of a righteous father ״רשיעא בר רשיעא״ is in line with רבי מאיר, who holds that a child's sin brings disgrace on the parent.

steps.title: What does 'This is the מצוה of the stoned' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line ״זו מצות הנסקלין״ and asks what this summary line is pointing back to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is the מצוה of those who are stoned.' What did the משנה teach, that it now says 'This is the מצוה of those who are stoned'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the line 'This is the מצוה of those who are stoned.' It then asks which earlier material in the משנה this line sums up, which sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A summary line like 'This is...' should point to something the משנה just described. The גמרא wants to pin down exactly what the word 'this' refers to. That opens a new topic after the discussion of רבי מאיר's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: the procedure (מצוה) for those executed by stoning
what did it teach, that it now teaches (this)?

phrases.english: The משנה says: 'This is the mitzva of those who are stoned.'
What did it teach, that it now teaches
'This is the מצוה of those who are stoned'?

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ מִצְוַת הַנִּסְקָלִין. מַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי מאיר discussion and goes back to analyze a line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier material in the משנה the summary line ״זו מצות הנסקלין״ refers to.

steps.title: The summary line closes the stoning section before burning begins
steps.stepSummary: The line ״זו מצות הנסקלין״ looks back at the whole earlier section on סקילה. It was said because the next משנה opens with מצות הנשרפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says this because it taught earlier: ״When the trial ends, they take him out to be stoned,″ and ״The place of stoning was two stories high.″ Since the next משנה wants to teach ״the מצוה of those who are burned,″ this one also says ״this is the מצוה of those who are stoned.″
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. The summary line points back to the earlier משנה about leading the condemned man out to be stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line does not add a new law. It closes the סקילה section so the משנה can move cleanly to a new type of execution, מצות הנשרפין. It is a matter of how the משנה is organized.

keyTerms.meaning: The trial has ended (with a guilty verdict)
Since / because (it is already saying something else)
The procedure for those executed by burning

phrases.english: Because it taught:
The trial has ended, they take him out to stone him.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי קוֹמוֹת.
phrases.english: The place of stoning was two stories high.
phrases.notes: Literally "two heights": twice the height of a person.

phrases.english: And since it wants to teach
the מצוה of those who are burned,
it also taught: "This is the מצוה of those who are stoned."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The line sums up the whole סקילה section, starting from ״נגמר הדין״. It is said because the next משנה starts מצות הנשרפין.

steps.title: The משנה describes how execution by burning is done
steps.stepSummary: The person is held in place in dung and choked with cloths until his mouth opens. Then a lit wick is thrown inside and burns his insides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of those who are burned: They sink him in dung up to his knees. They put a rough cloth inside a soft one and wrap it around his neck. One person pulls one way and another pulls the other way until he opens his mouth. Then someone lights the wick and throws it into his mouth. It goes down inside him and burns his intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains step by step how שריפה is carried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שריפה here does not mean burning the body from the outside. The burning happens inside the body through the wick. The dung and the cloths only hold the person still and force the mouth open.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture a bonfire. In this משנה, שריפה is done by a burning wick inside the body, and the outside of the body is not burned.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The מצוה of those who are burned:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ מְשַׁקְּעִין אוֹתוֹ בַּזֶּבֶל עַד אַרְכוּבּוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: they would sink him in dung up to his knees,
and they put a rough cloth inside a soft one,
and wrap it around his neck.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ,
phrases.english: This one pulls toward himself and that one pulls toward himself,
until he opens his mouth.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַדְלִיק אֶת הַפְּתִילָה וְזוֹרְקָהּ לְתוֹךְ פִּיו,
phrases.english: And he lights the wick and throws it into his mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹרֶדֶת לְתוֹךְ מֵעָיו וְחוֹמֶרֶת אֶת בְּנֵי מֵעָיו.
phrases.english: and it goes down into his insides and burns his intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the new topic that step 5 said was coming
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שריפה is done by forcing the mouth open with cloths around the neck and throwing a lit wick inside, which burns the intestines.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says to open the mouth with tongs instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה worries that the choking may kill the person before the wick goes in. Then the מצוה of שריפה would not be done. So he says to open the mouth with tongs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If he died in their hands from the choking, they would not have fulfilled the מצוה of burning with him. Rather, one opens his mouth with tongs, against his will, lights the wick, and throws it into his mouth. It goes down inside him and burns his intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the method in the first part of the משנה. He gives a different way to open the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions agree that the wick burns the person from inside. They argue only about how to open the mouth. רבי יהודה rejects the cloths because the person might die from choking, and that would be חנק, not שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Died in their hands (before the proper execution was done)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: But if he,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person being choked with the cloths in the first opinion.

phrases.english: if he died in their hands,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מְקַיְּימִין בּוֹ מִצְוַת שְׂרֵיפָה,
phrases.english: they would not have fulfilled with him the מצוה of burning,
rather, one opens his mouth with tongs
against his will,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַדְלִיק אֶת הַפְּתִילָה וְזוֹרְקָהּ לְתוֹךְ פִּיו,
phrases.english: and he lights the wick and throws it into his mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹרֶדֶת לְתוֹךְ מֵעָיו וְחוֹמֶרֶת אֶת בְּנֵי מֵעָיו.
phrases.english: and it goes down into his insides and burns his intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion on how to open the mouth in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not choke the person, because if he dies from the choking the מצוה of שריפה is lost. Open his mouth with tongs instead.

steps.title: A story of a בת כהן burned with branches
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק tells of a בת כהן who sinned and was burned with bundles of branches around her. This suggests שריפה means real burning of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק said: There was an incident with a בת כהן who committed adultery. They surrounded her with bundles of branches and burned her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק brings a story as evidence. The story seems to show that שריפה is done by burning the whole body from the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions above agree that the burning is internal, with a wick. This story points to a completely different kind of שריפה, an outside fire. If the story is a good proof, it goes against both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, often brought as proof
A daughter of a כהן, whose punishment for adultery is שריפה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok said:
There was an incident with one daughter of a kohen who committed adultery,
and they surrounded her with bundles of vine branches and burned her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן צָדוֹק מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that points to a different method from steps 6-7
steps.raayaObject: That שריפה is done by burning the body from the outside
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case of a בת כהן burned with bundles of branches

steps.title: The חכמים reject the story: that court did not know the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the story proves nothing. The בית דין at that time was not expert in the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That happened because the court at that time was not expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push away רבי אלעזר בן צדוק's proof. They say that court acted wrongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story only proves the הלכה if the people in it acted correctly. The חכמים say that בית דין made a mistake, so the story cannot change the method taught in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: שריפה in the משנה is done with a burning wick placed inside the body. The story of a בת כהן burned with branches is rejected, because that בית דין did not know the הלכה.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה בָּקִי.
phrases.english: Because the court of that time was not expert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole story is rejected as a source for how שריפה is done
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The בית דין in the story did not know the הלכה, so what it did does not show the correct practice

steps.title: What kind of wick?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means by the פתילה thrown into the person's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the 'wick'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking a simple question: what is this פתילה? This sets up רב מתנה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a lit פתילה is thrown into the mouth, but it did not say what the wick is made of. A normal cloth wick would hardly burn someone's insides, so the גמרא wants to know exactly what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is the 'wick'?
phrases.notes: This is the lit wick the משנה said is thrown into the person's mouth (Step 6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה of שריפה, asking about a word from Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What material the פתילה in the משנה is made of.

steps.title: A wick made of lead
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה explains that the פתילה is made of lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה says: a wick of lead.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers the question: the "wick" is a strip of lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lead is shaped like a wick and goes down into the person's insides. This explains how something thrown into the mouth can burn the inside of the body while the outside stays untouched.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture a cloth wick here. The 'wick' is a piece of metal (lead).

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
A wick of lead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה פְּתִילָה שֶׁל אֲבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פתילה is made of lead.

steps.title: What is the source for this kind of burning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that שריפה is done this way, burning the inside and not the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source that שריפה means burning the inside, not burning the body in a fire. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says "באש תשרף", which sounds like a normal fire. The גמרא wants a source showing that the burning happens inside the person while the body stays whole.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the method, the גמרא asks for its source in the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק-based source that שריפה means burning the soul while the body stays whole.

steps.title: Learning from עדת קרח
steps.stepSummary: The word שריפה is used both for the death penalty and for עדת קרח. Just as עדת קרח's souls were burned while their bodies stayed whole, so too here.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned through 'burning' 'burning' from עדת קרח. Just as there it was a burning of the soul while the body stayed whole, so too here it is a burning of the soul while the body stays whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a גזירה שוה. The word "burning" appears in both places, so they work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדת קרח were burned by ה׳, yet their bodies stayed whole and only their life inside was burned out. Since the same word is used for the death penalty, שריפה also means burning inside while the body stays whole. This is why a lead wick is used rather than a pile of wood.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one case from another because the same word appears in both
The group of קרח, burned by ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for why שריפה in בית דין is done with a wick and not a bonfire.

phrases.english: It is learned from 'burning' 'burning' from the assembly of Korah.
phrases.notes: The word shows up in ויקרא 21:9 for the death penalty and in במדבר 17:4 for עדת קרח.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים,
phrases.english: Just as there it was a burning of the soul and the body remained whole,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים.
phrases.english: so too here, a burning of the soul and the body remains whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'מנא לן' of Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: שריפה in בית דין burns the inside while the body stays whole.
steps.raayaSupportSource: גזירה שוה of the word 'שריפה' from עדת קרח.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns it from the sons of אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a different source: a גזירה שוה from the burning of בני אהרן (נדב and אביהוא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: It is learned through 'burning' 'burning' from בני אהרן. Just as there it was a burning of the soul while the body stayed whole, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר agrees with the rule but learns it from a different story: the deaths of נדב and אביהוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The result is the same: the soul is burned and the body stays whole. Only the source changes, from עדת קרח to בני אהרן, where the word "burning" is also used.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of אהרן, נדב and אביהוא, burned by ה׳

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
It is learned from 'burning' 'burning' from the sons of Aaron,
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 10:6, about the burning of נדב and אביהוא.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים –
phrases.english: just as there it was a burning of the soul and the body remained whole,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שְׂרֵיפַת נְשָׁמָה וְגוּף קַיָּים.
phrases.english: so too here, a burning of the soul and the body remains whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר אָתְיָא שְׂרֵיפָה שְׂרֵיפָה מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule given in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שריפה is learned from בני אהרן: the soul is burned and the body stays whole.

steps.title: How do we know עדת קרח's bodies stayed whole?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the one who learns from עדת קרח how he knows their bodies were not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who learns it from עדת קרח, from where does he know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the first source. It asks how we know that עדת קרח were burned only inside and not in their whole body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה only works if עדת קרח really died with their bodies whole. So the גמרא needs proof of that fact about עדת קרח itself.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּיָלֵיף מֵעֲדַת קֹרַח, מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: The one who learns it from the assembly of Korah, from where does he know it?
phrases.notes: He is asking how we know that עדת קרח's bodies were not burned up.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּיָלֵיף מֵעֲדַת קֹרַח מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first source (Step 13) to check its basis.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that עדת קרח's bodies stayed whole.

steps.title: They sinned 'with their souls'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the firepans of those who sinned "בנפשתם", meaning with their souls. This shows that only their souls were burned and their bodies stayed whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And the firepans of these sinners with their souls," which teaches that their souls were burned while their bodies stayed whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about עדת קרח that uses the word "בנפשתם", which means "with their souls".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נפש is read as pointing to the soul. That is what was burned, while the body stayed whole. This supports the גזירה שוה from Step 13.
steps.whatToRemember: שריפה in בית דין burns the inside with a lead wick while the body stays whole. This is learned by a גזירה שוה from עדת קרח (supported by the word בנפשתם) or, according to רבי אלעזר, from בני אהרן.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And the firepans of these sinners
phrases.notes: במדבר 17:3

phrases.english: with their souls,"
meaning that their souls were burned and the body remained whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וְאֵת מַחְתּוֹת הַחַטָּאִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּנַפְשֹׁתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'בנפשתם' shows that only the souls of עדת קרח were burned and their bodies stayed whole.

steps.title: The other view: עדת קרח were really burned
steps.stepSummary: The one who learns from בני אהרן says עדת קרח's bodies really burned, and reads 'בנפשתם' as 'because of their souls' cravings.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion? That was real burning. So what does 'with their souls' mean? That they became liable to burning because of matters of their souls (their bodily desires).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אלעזר, who does not learn from עדת קרח, deals with the word 'בנפשתם'. He answers that עדת קרח's bodies really were burned, and the word means something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the proof rested on reading 'בנפשתם' as 'only their souls were burned.' Here that reading is pushed aside: 'בנפשתם' means they were punished because of their נפש, their bodily appetites. Once the word is read this way, it no longer proves the bodies stayed whole.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does the other opinion explain this?
Actual, full burning of the body
Because of matters of their souls, meaning their bodily cravings

phrases.english: And the other one? That was actual burning.
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רבי אלעזר from step 14, who learns from בני אהרן instead.

phrases.english: And what does 'with their souls' mean?
That they became liable to burning
over matters of their souls.
phrases.notes: 'Souls' here means their appetites, food and drink, as the next step shows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the step 16 reading of 'בנפשתם' that the עדת קרח proof depended on
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from עדת קרח, not the halacha of how שריפה is done
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'בנפשתם' can mean 'because of their appetites' rather than 'only their souls were burned'

steps.title: Support from ריש לקיש: they flattered קרח for food
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains a פסוק in תהלים to mean that people flattered קרח because he fed them, and so גיהנם gnashed its teeth at them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like ריש לקיש, who said: What does the פסוק mean, 'With the flattering mockeries of cake, they gnash their teeth at me'? Because of the flattery they gave קרח over food, the minister of גיהנם gnashed his teeth at them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש to back up the reading from step 17. It shows that עדת קרח really did sin because of their appetites.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads 'מעוג' as coming from 'עוגה', a cake. Those people sided with קרח because he gave them food and drink. This fits reading 'בנפשתם' as 'because of their appetites.'

keyTerms.meaning: The minister (angel) in charge of גיהנם

phrases.english: Like Reish Lakish,
for Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'With the flattering mockeries of cake
phrases.notes: תהלים 35:16. 'מעוג' is being read as 'עוגה', a cake.

phrases.english: they gnash their teeth at me'?
Because of the flattery with which they flattered Korach
over matters of eating,

phrases.aramaic: חָרַק עֲלֵיהֶן שַׂר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שִׁנָּיו.
phrases.english: the minister of Gehinnom gnashed his teeth at them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the step 17 reading that עדת קרח sinned over their appetites
steps.raayaObject: The reading of 'בנפשתם' as 'because of their appetites'

steps.title: How does the בני אהרן side know their bodies stayed whole?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי אלעזר and asks how he knows that נדב ואביהוא were not burned on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who learns from the sons of אהרן, how does he know it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא questions the second source. It is setting up the next step by asking how we know the bodies of בני אהרן were not burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה from בני אהרן only works if their bodies stayed whole. So the גמרא asks for the proof of that fact, the same way it asked about עדת קרח in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And the one who learns it from the sons of Aharon
from where does he know it?
phrases.notes: He means: how does he know their bodies weren't burned?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּיָלֵיף מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 15, now questioning the בני אהרן source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that בני אהרן's bodies stayed whole

steps.title: 'And they died': like a normal death
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'וימותו', which suggests a death like a natural one, with the body left whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it is written: 'And they died before ה׳': like a normal death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19 with the word 'וימותו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have just said the fire burned them. Saying 'they died' hints that it looked like an ordinary death, where the body stays whole. So only the inside was burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Like an ordinary death, with the body intact

phrases.english: For it is written: 'And they died before ה׳,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:2

phrases.english: like a normal death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וימותו' shows their death looked like a natural death, so the body was whole

steps.title: The other view: בני אהרן were really burned
steps.stepSummary: The one who learns from עדת קרח says נדב ואביהוא were really burned. 'וימותו' only means the fire started inside them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? That was real burning. And what about 'and they died'? It means the fire started in them from inside, like a normal death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first opinion's answer. It explains 'וימותו' without proving that the bodies stayed whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion agrees the death was 'like a normal death,' but only in that it began from the inside, the way a natural death does. The burning itself was real burning. So 'וימותו' does not prove the bodies stayed whole, and the proof from בני אהרן is pushed aside.

keyTerms.meaning: It started in them from the inside

phrases.english: And the other one? That was actual burning.
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is the opinion from step 13, who learns from עדת קרח.

phrases.english: And what about what is written, 'and they died'?
That it started in them from inside,
like a normal death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the step 20 reading of 'וימותו', mirroring step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from בני אהרן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'וימותו' can mean the fire began inside, not that the body stayed whole

steps.title: ברייתא: threads of fire entered their noses
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי teaches that threads of fire went into the noses of נדב ואביהוא and burned them, showing the fire started from inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says: Two threads of fire came out of the קודש הקדשים, split into four, two went into the nose of one and two into the nose of the other, and they burned them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support step 21's claim that the fire started inside נדב ואביהוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire entered through their noses, so the burning really did begin on the inside. That supports the view that 'וימותו' points to how the fire entered, not to a body left untouched. The next step brings a challenge from another word in the same פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side keeps its own proof and pushes back on the other's. One reads 'בנפשתם' as 'because of their appetites.' The other reads 'וימותו' as 'the fire started inside.' Both agree that שריפה as a death penalty burns the inside.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Abba Yosei ben Dostai says:
Two threads of fire
came out of the Holy of Holies
and split into four,
and two went into the nose of this one
and two into the nose of that one
and burned them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 21's claim that the fire started inside them
steps.raayaObject: That the fire of בני אהרן started from inside their bodies
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי

steps.title: The verse says the fire 'ate them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that נדב ואביהוא were really burned. The פסוק says the fire 'ate them', and 'them' sounds like it leaves something out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And it devoured them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that the fire really burned נדב ואביהוא, body and all. It points to a פסוק that says the fire 'ate them'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Them' sounds like a limiting word: the fire ate them and nothing else. But if everything was burned up, what is the word leaving out? That seems to clash with the view that the fire really burned them, bones and flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written: a formula for challenging with a פסוק

phrases.english: But it is written: "And it devoured them"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:2. This is the fire that came out and killed נדב ואביהוא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of steps 21–22 that the fire, starting inside, really burned נדב ואביהוא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נדב ואביהוא were not burned on the outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'The fire ate them' suggests the bodies themselves were consumed.

steps.title: The fire ate them, but not their clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'them' means the people themselves, not their clothes. So the word leaves out their clothes, and their bodies could still have really burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It devoured 'them', but not their clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The fire 'ate them', meaning it burned the people, but it did not touch their clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Them' leaves out their clothes. The fire, which went in through their noses, burned the people themselves, but their clothes were not burned. So the word does not show that their bodies stayed whole.

phrases.english: "Them," and not their clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from 'ותאכל אותם'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrow reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The fire ate them' means their whole bodies were burned up from outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Them' means only the people, not their clothes. So the burning was internal and the outside stayed whole.

steps.title: Why not learn from the burned bulls?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't learn the method of שריפה from the פרים הנשרפים, which are actually burned up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from the bulls that are burned: just as there it is real burning, so too here it should be real burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we learn the death penalty of שריפה from the deaths of people (עדת קרח or בני אהרן) at all. Why not learn it from the פרים הנשרפים, which are fully burned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we learned from the bulls, the death penalty of שריפה would mean real, outside burning of the body. That would go against learning from the human cases (עדת קרח or בני אהרן), where the body stayed whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Bull offerings that are burned outside the camp

phrases.english: And let us learn from the bulls that are burned:
just as there it is actual burning,
so too here, it should be actual burning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the whole approach of learning שריפה from cases of people (עדת קרח or נדב ואביהוא).
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the method of שריפה from the death of people burned by fire from heaven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burned bulls are another case of שריפה in the תורה, and there the burning is real and complete.

steps.title: A person is better learned from a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it makes more sense to learn from a case about a person, since it shares more features with the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that one should learn from a person, since it shares: a person, a sinner, a soul, and פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that it is more logical to learn the death penalty from a case where a person died. It lists the things the two cases share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty and the human cases (עדת קרח or בני אהרן) both involve a person, a sinner, and a soul being taken. Also, the laws of פיגול apply to the bulls but not to people. So the case of a person is the closer match.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it stands to reason
An offering made invalid by the wrong intent about when it will be eaten

phrases.english: It makes sense that one should learn from a person,
since it is a person, a sinner,
a soul, and piggul.
phrases.notes: פיגול works the other way: it applies to the bulls but not to a person, so the person cases match each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why we don't learn from the burned bulls.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the closer comparison by counting shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learn from the bulls, so שריפה would mean real outside burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Learn from people, since they share more features with the death penalty.

steps.title: On the contrary, the bulls are a better match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the bulls match better, since they enable a מצוה and apply for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, one should learn from the bulls that are burned, since they enable something and apply for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument around. It says the bulls are actually the better match for the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burned bulls and the death penalty are both a מצוה that brings a result (the bulls bring כפרה, the death penalty carries out the law). Both are rules for all generations. נדב ואביהוא and עדת קרח were one-time events and not a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Enables, makes something fit or complete

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִפָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף,
phrases.english: On the contrary, one should learn from the bulls that are burned,
since they enable and are for all generations.
phrases.notes: These are two separate points: both are a מצוה that brings a result, and both are rules that last forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִפָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of the previous step by offering shared features on the other side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a person should be learned from a person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bulls share legal features with the death penalty: both are a מצוה that brings a result and both apply for all generations. The cases of people were one-time events.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The גמרא now has reasons pointing both ways. The next step decides which comparison wins.

steps.title: The human cases share more features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the shared features between the death penalty and the human cases outnumber those shared with the bulls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those features are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 27. The features that the death penalty shares with the human cases are more than the ones it shares with the bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said the bulls match better because they enable a מצוה and apply for all generations. The גמרא replies that we count the matching features, and the human cases win on numbers. So we still learn from עדת קרח or בני אהרן and not from the פרים הנשרפים.
steps.whatToRemember: When two sources each match in some ways, the גמרא here picks the one with more shared features.

phrases.english: Those are more numerous.
phrases.notes: "Those" means the features the death penalty shares with the human cases from step 26.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by counting the shared features.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing the number of shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bulls match better because they enable a מצוה and apply for all generations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The human cases share more features in total, so we learn from them.

steps.title: Why not learn from the sons of Aaron?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the opinion that learns from עדת קרח does not learn from בני אהרן instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who learns from the congregation of קרח, why does he not learn from the sons of אהרן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the opinion that learns the burning method from עדת קרח. It asks why he skips over בני אהרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both עדת קרח and בני אהרן are human cases, so both seem to fit. The גמרא wants to know what makes this opinion choose one over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation of קרח, who were burned by fire from Heaven
The sons of אהרן, נדב and אביהוא

phrases.english: The one who learns from the congregation of Korah,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא יָלֵיף מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he does not learn from the sons of Aaron?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּיָלֵיף מֵעֲדַת קֹרַח, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא יָלֵיף מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting that we learn from human cases, the גמרא asks why one opinion picks עדת קרח over בני אהרן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason this opinion does not use בני אהרן as the source.

steps.title: The sons of Aaron were actually burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in this opinion's view, בני אהרן were really burned up, so they cannot teach the inner burning method.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was actual burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains this opinion's reason. He holds that נדב and אביהוא were burned for real, bodies and all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method we want to learn is burning on the inside while the body stays whole. If בני אהרן were burned up completely, their case does not show that method. So this opinion uses עדת קרח instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Actual, full burning of the body

phrases.english: That was actual burning.
phrases.notes: "That" is the death of the sons of אהרן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: This opinion holds that בני אהרן were fully burned, so they do not show the inner burning method.

steps.title: Then learn actual burning from them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if בני אהרן were really burned, we should learn from them that execution means real, full burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the sons of אהרן were truly burned up, why not copy that and burn the condemned person fully?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 used the full burning of בני אהרן as a reason to set them aside. The גמרא flips it: that same fact could teach that שריפה should be full burning. So why prefer the inner method learned from עדת קרח?

keyTerms.meaning: Then let us learn from it

phrases.english: So let us learn from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 30 into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to learn from עדת קרח rather than from בני אהרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בני אהרן were really burned, they are a valid source for full burning, so why not follow them?

steps.title: Choose a kind death for him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers from the פסוק ואהבת לרעך כמוך: we must pick a kind death even for the condemned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The פסוק says, "And you shall love your neighbor as yourself," which teaches: choose for him a nice death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why we do not learn full burning from בני אהרן. The תורה tells us to love our neighbor, so even a condemned person gets the kindest death possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Given two possible sources, we pick the one that gives a gentler death. The inner burning learned from עדת קרח is quicker and less painful than burning the whole body. So ואהבת לרעך כמוך decides in favor of עדת קרח.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose for him a nice (kind) death

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, בְּרוֹר לוֹ מִיתָה יָפָה, is a basic principle in how בית דין carries out the death penalty: even then, we must act with care for the person.
steps.confusionAlert: "A nice death" does not mean the punishment is cancelled. The person is still executed; the rule only shapes how, so it is as gentle as possible.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The verse said: "And you shall love your neighbor as yourself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: choose for him a nice death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אָמַר קְרָא ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing an outside principle that decides between two possible sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בני אהרן were fully burned, maybe execution should be full burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: ואהבת לרעך כמוך tells us to pick the kinder death, so we follow the inner burning learned from עדת קרח.

steps.title: Why do we need the גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רב נחמן's rule already tells us to pick the kinder death, why do we need the גזירה שוה to learn the method?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since there is the teaching of רב נחמן, why do I need the גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. If ואהבת לרעך כמוך already leads us to the gentle inner burning, the גזירה שוה from earlier seems unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the method of שריפה was learned through a גזירה שוה linking it to a source. Now רב נחמן's rule seems to reach the same result by itself. The גמרא asks what the גזירה שוה adds, setting up the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from a shared word in two places

phrases.english: And since there is the teaching of Rav Naḥman,
why do I need the verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאִיכָּא דְּרַב נַחְמָן, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 32 to question whether the earlier גזירה שוה is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the גזירה שוה as a source for the burning method.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ואהבת לרעך כמוך already brings us to the gentle method, the גזירה שוה seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Without the analogy, inner burning would not count as burning at all
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה is needed to teach that burning the soul while the body stays whole counts as שריפה. Without it, ואהבת לרעך כמוך would only tell us to burn the body more quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the גזירה שוה, I would have said that burning the soul while the body stays whole is not burning at all. And because of 'love your neighbor as yourself,' they should just add more bundles of branches so he burns quickly. So the גזירה שוה teaches us that inner burning counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 33's question: why do we need the גזירה שוה if רב נחמן's kindness rule already exists?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ואהבת לרעך כמוך only tells us to pick the kindest way within what counts as real שריפה. It cannot decide what counts as שריפה in the first place. The גזירה שוה supplies that point: inner burning with the body left whole is a real form of שריפה, and then the kindness rule chooses it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned by linking the same word in two places in the תורה
I would have thought (an idea that later turns out to be wrong)
Burning of the soul while the body stays whole
Bundles of vine branches used as fuel

steps.whatToRemember: The kindness rule picks the gentlest method only among methods that count. The גזירה שוה is what makes inner burning count as שריפה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two sources overlap. The גזירה שוה defines what counts as שריפה, and ואהבת לרעך כמוך chooses the kindest option within that definition. Each one does a different job.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why בית דין performs שריפה by pouring molten lead inside the person instead of burning the body on a fire.

phrases.english: Were it not for the verbal analogy,
I would have said:
burning of the soul while the body stays whole
is not burning at all.
And if it is because of "Love your neighbor as yourself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: let them add more bundles of branches for him
so that he burns quickly.
So it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that each source does a separate job: one defines the category and the other picks the method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Inner burning with the body left whole is not שריפה, so kindness would only mean adding fuel to burn the body faster.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה makes inner burning count as שריפה, and then ואהבת לרעך כמוך tells us to choose it.

steps.title: נדב ואביהוא wonder when משה ואהרן will die
steps.stepSummary: An אגדה: while walking behind משה ואהרן, נדב said to אביהוא, 'When will these two old men die so we can lead?' הקב"ה answered, 'We shall see who buries whom.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Once משה ואהרן were walking on the road, with נדב ואביהוא behind them and all of ישראל behind them. נדב said to אביהוא: 'When will these two old men die, so that you and I can lead the generation?' הקב"ה said to them: 'We shall see who buries whom.'
steps.whatsHappening: Because בני אהרן came up in the discussion, the גמרא moves away from the הלכה and tells a story about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows a hidden wish in נדב ואביהוא to take over leadership. הקב"ה's answer points ahead to what really happened: the young sons died first, while משה ואהרן lived on.

phrases.english: And once Moshe and Aharon were
walking on the road,
and Nadav and Avihu were walking behind them,
and all of Israel behind them.
Nadav said to Avihu:
When will these two old men die
so that you and I will lead the generation?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
We shall see who buries whom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְבָר הָיוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן מְהַלְּכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הלכה discussion and opens a related אגדה about בני אהרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נדב ואביהוא hoped to replace משה ואהרן, but הקב"ה hinted that they would die first.

steps.title: רב פפא's saying about old and young camels
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the story matches a popular saying: many old camels end up carrying the skins of young camels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: 'Many old camels are loaded with the skins of young camels.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא connects the story of נדב ואביהוא to a well-known everyday saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying means that the young often die before the old, and the old end up carrying what is left of them. In the same way, the young נדב ואביהוא died while the old משה ואהרן were still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: A young person should not count on outliving the old. נדב ואביהוא died first, just as הקב"ה hinted.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
Many are the old camels
that are loaded with the skins of young camels.
phrases.notes: In other words, the young camels died first, and the old ones carry their hides.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the אגדה with a popular saying that fits the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young often die before the old, as happened with נדב ואביהוא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר begins a new teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement in the name of רבי אליעזר. His words continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. It introduces a teaching from רבי אליעזר, and the teaching itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The actual content of רבי אליעזר's statement comes right after this line. For now, we only know who is about to speak.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the אגדה about נדב ואביהוא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a statement of רבי אליעזר that continues in the next section.
